answer: I'd like to talk about a morning when I got up far earlier than I ever normally would. A time I got up unusually early was to watch the sunrise from a hilltop during a short trip to Bandarban with friends, about two years ago. We had to wake at around four in the morning, which was genuinely [[brutal]], especially as none of us are naturally early risers. The reason was simple: people had told us that the sunrise over the hills, with clouds drifting below you, was something you had to see at least once. Half asleep, we made the climb in the dark, questioning why we had agreed to it, with only our phone torches to guide us. Our guesthouse owner had kindly woken us with hot tea before we set off. It was surprisingly cold, and I remember wishing I had brought a thicker jacket. But the moment the sun began to rise over the horizon, all the tiredness [[melted away]]. The view was absolutely [[breathtaking]], with the sky shifting through shades of orange and pink, and a sea of clouds stretching out beneath us. It was a genuinely [[serene]] moment, and we stood there in near silence, simply taking it in. What made it so worthwhile was that we had earned that view through real effort. Honestly, that early start turned out to be the [[crowning moment]] of the whole trip. It taught me that sometimes the best moments require sacrificing a bit of comfort, and I would happily do it again.

followUps.q: Are you usually an early riser?
followUps.answer: Not naturally. On working days I get up around seven, which is early enough for me. At the weekend I try to sleep in a little, although the call to prayer usually wakes me anyway.

followUps.q: Do you think getting up early is good for people?
followUps.answer: For many people, yes. The morning is quiet and you can get a lot done before the day becomes busy. But I think it depends on the person, since some people genuinely work better at night.

note: Set in Bandarban with the sea-of-clouds sunrise; added the reason for waking early and the cold climb; plain 'memorable' replaced by 'highlight' and 'melted away'.
